summary: Configured node1 with a persistent HTTP backend on TCP 8091 and a persistent TCP reverse proxy on 8090. Both return `backend-ready` and recovered successfully after a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Created and enabled `backend-8091.service`, serving HTTP responses from Python on 0.0.0.0:8091.
Created and enabled `reverse-proxy-8090.service`, using socat to proxy 0.0.0.0:8090 to node1:8091.
Verified direct and proxied responses before reboot.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its boot identity changed from 4eaf428d-1724-4431-a764-c9e0fdc350cc to f9af3214-0ab3-498f-9191-b4387db5bbd6.
Verified both services, listeners, and responses recovered after reboot with no failed systemd units.

evidence.requirement: Local backend on TCP 8091 returns backend-ready
evidence.summary: Direct requests to node1:8091 returned exactly `backend-ready`; the Python service was active and listening before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Reverse proxy on TCP 8090 publishes the backend
evidence.summary: Requests to node1:8090 returned exactly `backend-ready`; evidence shows the socat listener and its node1:8091 upstream.

Captured healthy baseline and original boot ID, acknowledged the scheduled safe reboot, proved a changed boot ID, then verified system health, active/enabled services, both listeners, and direct/proxied responses.
